core_obligations: Identify the hom groups (proof lines 14031-14037): for every abelian sheaf G on Z_etale one has Hom_Z(G, H_Z(F)) = Hom_X(i_*G, F), because every section of i_*G has support in Z.

Use exactness of i_* (proof lines 14038-14039): since i_* is exact, an injective object I of Ab(X_etale) has exact contravariant hom functor after composition with i_*, so the composite functor G -> Hom_X(i_*G, I) is exact.
Conclude injectivity (proof lines 14039-14040): by the identification above the contravariant hom functor of H_Z(I) on Z_etale is that composite, hence exact, so H_Z(I) is injective on Z_etale.
proof_roadmap: Compute the hom groups into the sheaf of sections with support as hom groups into the injective sheaf along i_*.
Use exactness of i_* to inherit exactness of the hom functor.
Conclude injectivity of the sections with support on the closed subscheme.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the sheaf of sections with support in a closed subscheme is injective on the closed subscheme whenever the original sheaf is injective (statement lines 14022-14028). The proof identifies the hom functor of H_Z(I) on Z_etale with the composite G -> Hom_X(i_*G, I), using that every section of i_*G is supported in Z (proof lines 14031-14037), and then uses exactness of i_* together with injectivity of I to see that this composite is exact, which is the defining property of injectivity (proof lines 14038-14040). The claim is H2: one identification of representing functors plus one exactness input, with the adjunction serving as the construction of the sheaf.
